chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the cheese, so he said to me: 'You have asked me about a food that I love.' Then he gave the boy a dirham and said: 'O boy, buy us some cheese and call for the meal.' So we had lunch with him, and the cheese was brought. He ate and we ate with him. When we finished the meal, I said to him: 'What do you say about the cheese?' He said to me: 'Did you not see me eating it?' I said: 'Yes, but I like to hear it from you.' He said: 'I will inform you about the cheese and other things: everything that contains both permissible and prohibited elements is permissible for you until you recognize the prohibited part with your own eye, then you leave it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on food items that contain both halal and haram elements?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'al-asl al-suhha' (the default state of purity) for food, illustrating that mixed ingredients are permissible until the specific prohibited element is identified. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) combines practical demonstration with legal reasoning, showing that the presence of a minor prohibited component (like rennet from a non-Zabiha animal) does not render the entire food haram unless its distinct nature is known. This serves as a foundational text in Shia fiqh for resolving doubts regarding food ingredients in daily life.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the cheese, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘You have asked me<sup>asws</sup> about a food which I<sup>asws</sup> love’.  Then he<sup>asws</sup> gave one Dirham to the slave, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O slave! Buy some cheese for us and call for the lunch’. So we had lunch with him<sup>asws</sup>, and they came with the cheese. 
So he<sup>asws</sup> ate and we ate with him<sup>asws</sup>. So when we were free from the lunch, I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the cheese?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Or did you not see me<sup>asws</sup> eating it?’ I said, ‘Yes, but I would love to hear it from you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I shall inform you about the cheese and other such, everything what was Permissible regarding it, and Prohibited. So it is Permissible for you until you recognise the Prohibition with exactly it, so leave it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sulayman who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about cheese. He (the Imam) said, ’You have asked me about a food that is attractive to me. 5 He (the Imam) then gave a dirham to the boy and asked him to bring cheese. He (the Imam) asked for lunch which was brought. He (the Imam) ate and we ate with him (the Imam). When we finished lunch I asked, ‘What do you say about cheese? 5 He (the Imam) asked me, ‘Did you not see me eating it with you? 5 I replied, ‘Yes, I saw you but I like to hear it from you. 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘I will tell you about cheese and other things. Whatever has lawful in it as well as unlawful is lawful for you, until you learn that it particularly is unlawful, then you must leave it.’”
